observations: A large oval outline drawn in white frames a dense layered face-like form against a flat bright blue field; the oval sits slightly left of center.
Two inset shapes occupy the eye positions: a red heart pierced by a white bar on the left, and a yellow-green flower with a looped center on the right, each enclosed in its own rectangular boundary.

A wide open mouth near the bottom shows alternating black and white rectangular teeth under a pink zigzag lip line; loose yellow, black, and white scribble lines extend beyond the oval into all four corners.
reading: The face-like structure feels almost festive rather than threatening: a heart and a flower standing in for eyes give the layered form an oddly tender quality, even as the bared teeth and dense overlapping lines push toward agitation. The flat blue field keeps everything readable, holding the internal density at a distance. Two moods coexist without resolving.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #172 and nnxyz nnotb #174. Where #172 uses a dark green field with compressed shadowed forms, and #174 shifts to teal with angular eye shapes, #173 opens to flat sky blue with symbol-like eye forms.

connections.reason: Both works place a face-like oval on a flat bright blue field with loose scribble lines extending into the corners, making the shared blue ground and spatial layout the clearest formal link across the two owned collections.

Title neighbor nnxyz nnotb #172 shares the bared-teeth mouth structure and layered line density, but its dark green field and absence of symbol-like eye forms make the contrast in mood between the two works direct and visible.

lookingQuestion: What does the difference between the left eye shape and the right eye shape do to how you read the two halves of the face?
ambiguities: The small mark at lower right resembles a signature but its exact content is not legible at this resolution.

The rawblocks #59 comparison belongs to a different collection family; the formal blue-field link is visible in the inspected images but cross-collection context is limited to what can be seen directly.
